title: Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on the Utilization of Waterfront Areas
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on the Utilization of Waterfront Areas and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Extent of Waterfront Areas)
The "proportion prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Special Act on the Utilization of Waterfront Areas (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means 50 percent.

Article 3 (Size of Waterfront Areas)
(1) The "size prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the second sentence of Article 4(1) of the Act means 100,000 square meters. However, it means 30,000 square meters in an area falling under Article 12(1)1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Balanced Regional Development and Fostering of Local Small and Medium Enterprises.
(2) The requirements in the proviso to paragraph (1) shall apply by administrative district of a Si (including a Special Metropolitan City and a Metropolitan City) or Gun. Detailed matters, including specific calculation methods, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended March 23, 2013; December 30, 2014; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 4 (Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may, in consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, determine and publicly notify standards necessary for preparing and drawing up a plan for a waterfront area development project under Article 4(2) and (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "project plan"). <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) A person intending to propose designation of a waterfront area under Article 4(3) of the Act shall submit a proposal for designation of a waterfront area, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, attaching the following documents and drawings: <Amended July 20, 2012; March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. A location map at a scale of 1:25,000.
2. A topographic map at a scale of 1:5,000 showing the boundaries of the waterfront area and the reasons for determining them.
3. Survey documents on the status of farmland and forest land to be included in the waterfront area.
4. Documents stating the location, lot number, land category, area, details of ownership and rights other than ownership in the land, buildings, other objects or rights under Article 3 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land and Other Property for Public Works Projects to be expropriated or used, and the names (for corporations, corporate names) and addresses of their owners and right holders.
5. Documents necessary for a strategic environmental impact assessment under Articles 11, 12 and 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
(3) Upon receiving documents and drawings under paragraph (2), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall check the cadastral maps and forest land maps of the waterfront area through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(4) A person intending to propose modification of a waterfront area under Article 4(3) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment a proposal for modification of a waterfront area, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, attaching the documents and drawings necessary for the modification. A person intending to propose cancellation of a waterfront area under that paragraph shall submit to the Minister a proposal for cancellation of a waterfront area, as prescribed by Ordinance of that Ministry, attaching a statement of the reasons for cancellation. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(5) "Modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the provisos to Article 4(5) and (6) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Increasing or decreasing the area of a waterfront area by less than 10 percent.
2. Correcting an area that is erroneous or omitted.

Article 5 (Basic Directions for Development of Waterfront Areas)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 5, subparagraph 5 of the Act means the following matters: <Amended June 15, 2015; May 7, 2024>
1. Access to the river and connections with the river shall be maximized.
2. Utilization of new energy and renewable energy under Article 2, subparagraphs 1 and 2 of the Act on Promotion of Development, Use and Dissemination of New Energy and Renewable Energy shall be maximized.
3. For areas requiring water quality conservation, such as riparian zones, the purpose of their designation shall not be impaired.
4. Areas with high conservation value, in consideration of the natural environment, national heritage and similar factors, shall be preserved in their original state to the greatest extent possible.

Article 6 (Matters to Be Included in Project Plans)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 6, subparagraph 10 of the Act means the following matters: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. A support plan for installation of major infrastructure, including trunk facilities under Article 18 of the Act.
2. A plan for supply of integrated energy.
3. Other matters that the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment considers necessary in light of the functions of the waterfront area development project under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act.

Article 7 (Hearing Opinions of Residents and Others)
(1) "Important matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 7(1) of the Act means any of the following matters:
1. Modification of the principal functions of a waterfront area development project under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act.
2. An increase or decrease of at least 10 percent in the area designated as a waterfront area.
(2) To hear the opinions of residents, relevant experts and others (hereinafter referred to as "residents and others") under the main clause of Article 7(1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall send copies of the relevant documents to the competent head of a Si/Gun/Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) Upon receiving the relevant documents under paragraph (2), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall, without delay, publicly announce the following matters in a daily newspaper whose principal circulation area is the relevant area, and in the official bulletin, website and similar media of the relevant local government, and make the documents available for public inspection for 14 days from the announcement:
1. The name, location and area of the waterfront area.
2. The period and method for inspection of the relevant documents.
(4) A person having an opinion on the matters announced under paragraph (3) may submit it to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu during the inspection period under paragraph (3)2 (hereinafter referred to as the "inspection period").
(5) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving opinions under paragraph (4) shall compile them and submit them to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment without delay after the inspection period ends. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(6) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall examine whether to reflect opinions submitted under paragraph (5) in designation or modification of the waterfront area, and notify the persons who submitted the opinions of the results within 60 days from the end of the inspection period or receipt of the opinions from the head of a Si/Gun/Gu. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(7) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) through (6), in either of the following cases the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may directly hear the opinions of residents and others, or have the relevant Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor or Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") hear the opinions at that Mayor/Do Governor's request: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. Where the waterfront area extends across the jurisdictions of two or more Si/Gun/Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply).
2. Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving the relevant documents under paragraph (2) fails to make the announcement under paragraph (3).
(8) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or a Mayor/Do Governor hears the opinions of residents and others under paragraph (7), paragraph (2) (excluding cases where the Minister directly hears the opinions) and paragraphs (3) through (6) shall apply mutatis mutandis. In such cases, "head of a Si/Gun/Gu" shall be construed as "Mayor/Do Governor." <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(9) When hearing the opinions of residents and others under paragraphs (2) through (8), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may also hear the opinions of interested parties, including residents, relevant experts, environmental organizations and civic organizations, concerning a strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 13 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. <Amended July 20, 2012; March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 8 (Public Notice of Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) When the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment prepares a project plan and designates a waterfront area under Article 4(1) and the main clause of Article 4(2) of the Act, the Minister shall publish notice of the following matters in the Official Gazette under Article 8(1) of the Act: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The name, location and area of the waterfront area.
2. The date of designation of the waterfront area.
3. The name, location and representative's name of the implementer of the waterfront area development project under Article 12(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "project implementer").
4. The name of the project (including the functions of the waterfront area development project under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply).
5. The land use plan and major infrastructure plan.
6. The support plan for installation of major infrastructure necessary for development of the waterfront area.
7. The location, lot number, land category, area, details of ownership and rights other than ownership in land, buildings, other objects or rights to be expropriated or used, and the names (for corporations, corporate names) and addresses of their owners and right holders.
8. The method of inspection of the relevant documents.
9. Topographic drawings under Article 8(2) of the Framework Act on Land Use Regulation.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), in cases under the proviso to Article 4(2) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice of the matters in paragraph (1)1 and 2 when designating the waterfront area, and of the matters in each subparagraph of paragraph (1) when preparing the project plan. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(3) When modifying a waterfront area or a project plan, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice of the modified matters among those in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) and the reasons for modification. When cancelling designation of a waterfront area, the Minister shall publish notice of the cancellation and its reasons. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 9 (Activities Subject to Permission)
(1) "Activities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the first sentence of Article 9(1) of the Act means any of the following activities: <Amended July 2, 2019>
1. Construction and similar activities involving buildings: construction (including construction and erection of temporary buildings), major repair, or change of use of a building under Article 2(1)2 of the Building Act.
2. Installation of structures: installation of artificially manufactured facilities (excluding buildings under Article 2(1)2 of the Building Act).
3. Change of the form and quality of land: activities changing the shape of land by cutting (excavating soil), filling (piling soil), grading (leveling land), paving (covering with soil) or similar methods, excavation (digging) of land, or reclamation of public waters.
4. Extraction of soil or stone: extraction of soil, sand, gravel, rocks and similar material (excluding cases for the purpose of changing the form and quality of land under subparagraph 3).
5. Subdivision or merger of land.
6. Stockpiling of objects: stockpiling objects that are difficult to move for at least one month.
7. Felling or planting bamboo and trees: digging up, cutting down or planting bamboo and trees.
8. Newly cultivating or growing perennial plants.
(2) When granting permission for an activity in any subparagraph of paragraph (1), if a project implementer has been designated for the relevant area under Article 12 of the Act, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall first hear that project implementer's opinion.
(3) "Activities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 9(2)2 of the Act means any of the following activities that are not subject to permission for development activities under Article 56 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act:
1. Change of the form and quality of land for cultivation (limited to cases not involving a change of land category).
2. Extraction of soil or stone within a scope that neither hinders development of the waterfront area nor impairs the natural landscape.
3. Stockpiling objects on a site determined to be retained in its original state within the waterfront area.
(4) A person required to report under Article 9(3) of the Act shall, within 30 days from public notice of designation of the waterfront area, report to the competent head of a Si/Gun/Gu by submitting the report prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment with the following documents and other materials attached: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. Documents proving permissions and reported matters under relevant statutes.
2. Documents and photographs showing construction progress.
3. Design documents (limited to cases under paragraph (1)2).
4. Drawings and documents relating to the construction or project, including layout plans (limited to cases under paragraph (1)3 and 4).

Article 10 (Cancellation of Designation of Waterfront Areas)
(1) Where designation of a waterfront area is cancelled under Article 11(1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publish notice of the following matters in the Official Gazette and send the relevant documents to the heads of relevant administrative agencies and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The name of the waterfront area whose designation is cancelled.
2. The location and area of the waterfront area whose designation is cancelled.
3. Whether the specific-use area under Article 36 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act is restored to its former designation.
(2) Upon receiving the relevant documents under paragraph (1), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall, without delay, publicly announce their contents in the relevant local government's official bulletin, website and similar media, and make the contents available for public inspection for 14 days from the announcement.

Article 11 (Entrustment of Waterfront Area Development Projects)
(1) A project implementer may entrust land acquisition, compensation for losses, relocation measures and facility operation affairs of a waterfront area development project to any of the following persons under Article 12(4) of the Act. However, only facility operation affairs may be entrusted to a person falling under subparagraph 5.
1. The State or a local government.
2. A public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions.
3. A local public corporation established under the Local Public Enterprises Act.
4. A corporation established for the purpose of carrying out waterfront area development projects, with all or part of its capital contributed by a project implementer under Article 12(1)2 or 3 of the Act.
5. A corporation operating cultural, tourism, leisure or similar facilities.
(2) When entrusting a waterfront area development project under paragraph (1), the project implementer shall consult with the entrusted party on the following matters:
1. An outline of the entrusted project.
2. The period (including the construction commencement date and scheduled completion date) and construction schedule of the entrusted project.
3. Procurement, management and execution of the costs of the entrusted project.
4. The method of implementation of the entrusted project.
5. The bearing of risks.
6. Treatment of property arising from implementation of the entrusted project.
(3) A project implementer intending to entrust part of a waterfront area development project under paragraph (1) shall report the entrustment to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment before entrusting it. In such cases, the Minister shall determine the necessity of entrustment by comprehensively considering the details of the project to be entrusted, the entrusted party's ability to perform the project and similar factors, and notify the project implementer of the result within 14 days from receipt of the report. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 12 (Execution of Waterfront Area Development Projects on Behalf of Project Implementers)
(1) A person intending to execute part of a waterfront area development project on behalf of the project implementer under Article 12(4) of the Act shall submit to the project implementer an application for execution of a waterfront area development project on the implementer's behalf, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, stating the following matters: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The name (for a corporation, its name and its representative's name) and address of the person intending to execute the project on the implementer's behalf.
2. The name and location of the waterfront area where the person intends to execute the project on the implementer's behalf, and the area of such execution.
3. An outline of the implementation plan for execution of the waterfront area development project on the implementer's behalf, including:
(a) The purpose of the project.
(b) The type and outline of the project.
(c) The project implementation period.
(2) The following documents and drawings shall be attached to the application under paragraph (1):
1. A location map.
2. A project plan.
3. A financing plan.
(3) A project implementer intending to have another person execute part of a waterfront area development project on the implementer's behalf shall conclude a contract with that person for such execution.
(4) The project implementer shall guide and supervise the person contracted under paragraph (3) to ensure faithful implementation of the project in accordance with the contract.
(5) Article 11(3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports concerning execution on behalf of the project implementer and to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment's examination and notification thereof. In such cases, "entrustment" and "entrusted party" in Article 11(3) shall be construed as "execution on behalf of the project implementer" and "person who will execute the project on the implementer's behalf," respectively. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 13 (Implementation Plans for Waterfront Area Development Projects)
(1) A project implementer intending to obtain approval of an implementation plan for a waterfront area development project under Article 13(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") shall submit to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment an application for approval of an implementation plan, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, stating the following matters: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The purpose of the project.
2. The method of project implementation.
3. The current status of land use.
4. The matters in Article 13(4)1 through 3, 5 and 7 of the Act.
(2) The following documents and drawings shall be attached when submitting the application for approval of an implementation plan under paragraph (1): <Amended April 10, 2012>
1. A location map.
2. A detailed list of buildings and other structures intended to be retained in the waterfront area.
3. Relevant documents and drawings necessary for a decision on an urban/Gun management plan (including a district-unit plan).
(3) When intending to approve an implementation plan (including approval of a modification) under the main clause of Article 13(2) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall check the cadastral maps and forest land maps through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(4) "Modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 13(2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. A change of the project implementer's address.
2. A change of the representative of a project implementer that is a corporation.
3. Correction of the area of a waterfront area due to an error or similar cause within a scope that does not change its boundaries.
4. Division of a project without changing the area of the waterfront area or the functions of the waterfront area development project under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act.
5. An increase or decrease of less than 10 percent in the area of the waterfront area.
(5) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 13(4)11 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Details of land, buildings, other objects or rights in the waterfront area, acquisition and compensation, and measures for relocation of residents.
2. A plan for free vesting and replacement of public facilities, land and similar property.
3. A plan for execution of the waterfront area development project on behalf of the project implementer (only if such a plan exists).
(6) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may determine and publicly notify standards necessary for preparation of implementation plans. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 14 (Public Notice of Approval of Implementation Plans)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 13(5) of the Act means the following matters: <Amended January 26, 2021>
1. The name of the project.
2. The project implementer's name (for a corporation, its name and its representative's name).
3. The purpose and outline of the project.
4. The location and area of the waterfront area.
5. The project implementation period (including the scheduled construction commencement and completion dates).
6. The matters in each subparagraph of Article 25(6) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.

Article 15 (Special Cases for Housing Supply)
"Areas prescribed by Presidential Decree where speculation is feared" in Article 17(2) of the Act means the following areas: <Amended August 11, 2016>
1. Areas designated under Article 104-2(1) of the Income Tax Act.
2. Overheated speculation zones under Article 63 of the Housing Act.

Article 16 (Completion Inspection)
(1) A project implementer intending to undergo a completion inspection under Article 20(1) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment a construction completion report, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, stating the following matters: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The project implementer's name (for a corporation, its name and its representative's name) and address.
2. The name of the project.
3. The location and area of the waterfront area.
4. The project implementation period.
5. The land use plan.
6. The infrastructure installation plan.
(2) The following documents and drawings shall be attached to the construction completion report under paragraph (1): <Amended March 23, 2013; August 31, 2016; June 8, 2018; January 21, 2022; October 1, 2025>
1. A completion statement (including as-built design documents and completion photographs).
2. A cadastral survey result map issued by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu.
3. An application for supply of land, buildings, structures or other property developed through the waterfront area project under Article 22 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "developed land and other property").
4. A statement of vesting of public facilities, land and similar property under Article 24 of the Act (including an appraisal statement by an appraisal corporation or similar entity under the Act on Appraisal and Certified Appraisers concerning public facilities, land and similar property whose use has been discontinued, and an itemized calculation of the construction costs of newly installed public facilities; however, this shall not apply where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment recognizes that the installation costs of newly installed public facilities exceed the appraised value of the public facilities whose use has been discontinued), and drawings.
(3) Upon receiving a construction completion report under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall set a completion inspection schedule and notify the head of the State agency or local government that will take over or manage the public facilities included in the report at least five days before the inspection date. A State agency or local government head wishing to participate in the completion inspection shall request participation no later than the day before the completion inspection date. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 17 (Use of Developed Land and Other Property Before Completion)
(1) A person who has acquired developed land and other property and intends to obtain permission for use before completion under Article 20(4) of the Act shall submit to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment the application prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
(2) Upon receiving an application for use before completion under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall grant permission for such use unless the Minister considers it to hinder the waterfront area development project. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 18 (Public Announcement of Completion of Construction)
The public announcement of completion of construction under Article 21 of the Act shall be made by announcing the following matters in the Official Gazette:
1. The name of the project.
2. The project implementer's name (for a corporation, its name and its representative's name) and address.
3. The location and area of the waterfront area.
4. The year, month and day of the completion inspection.
5. The plan for management and disposal of developed land and other property.

Article 19 (Application for Approval of Supply of Developed Land and Other Property)
(1) To obtain the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment's approval for supply of developed land and other property under Article 22 of the Act, a project implementer shall submit to the Minister an application for supply approval, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, stating the following matters and attaching a subdivision drawing of the developed land and other property to be supplied: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The location, area and intended supply use of the developed land and other property to be supplied.
2. Eligibility requirements for recipients and their selection method.
3. The timing, method and conditions of supply.
4. The method for determining the supply price.
5. The method and contents of the supply announcement.
6. Other matters that the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment determines to be necessary and publicly notifies.
(2) Upon receiving an application for supply approval from a project implementer under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall decide whether to approve it and notify the project implementer within 30 days from receipt. <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 20 (Advance Payments)
To receive advance payments under Article 23 of the Act, a project implementer shall obtain approval of the implementation plan under Article 13 of the Act.

Article 21 (Payment of the Sale Price of State and Public Property)
(1) The State and local governments may allow the sale price of State or public property sold to a project implementer under Article 25(4) of the Act to be paid in installments over a period of up to 20 years. In such cases, the interest applied to the unpaid balance of the sale price shall not exceed four percent per annum.
(2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), payment of the sale price of State and public property shall be governed by the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.

Article 22 (Application Mutatis Mutandis to Projects Outside Waterfront Areas)
(1) A project directly related to a waterfront area development project under Article 26 of the Act shall be any of the following projects: <Amended January 17, 2017>
1. A project for roads, railways, marina harbors, water supply, sewerage, public wastewater treatment facilities, waste treatment facilities, or electricity, broadcasting or telecommunications facilities.
2. A project for gas or oil supply facilities.
3. A river improvement project.
4. A project for extraction of soil or stone or dredging a river for a waterfront area development project.
(2) Where a project implementer carries out a project in any subparagraph of paragraph (1) in an area near a waterfront area, the second sentence of Article 4(4), Article 9, Articles 13 through 21, Articles 24, 25, 27, 39 and 40, and Articles 42 through 44 of the Act shall apply mutatis mutandis. In such cases, "waterfront area" shall be construed as "area near the waterfront area where a project in any subparagraph of Article 22(1) is implemented," and "waterfront area development project" as "project directly related to a waterfront area development project."

Article 23 (Public Notice of Cancellation of Designation of Project Implementers)
When publishing notice in the Official Gazette of cancellation of designation of a project implementer or a similar measure under Article 27(2) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall specifically state the following matters: <Amended March 23, 2013; June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. The name of the project.
2. The project implementer's name and address and its representative's name.
3. The purpose and outline of the project.
4. The project implementation period.
5. The location and area of the waterfront area.
6. The reasons for cancellation or the similar measure.

Article 24 (Reasonable Profit)
"Reasonable profit prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 31(2)4 of the Act means the amount calculated by the following formula:
| {A-(B+C+D)} [operator unidentifiable in the source text] (10/100) |
| A: The value of the land subject to assessment at the assessment termination point for waterfront area development gains under Article 31(1) of the Act. |
| B: The amount under Article 31(2)1 of the Act (the value of the land subject to assessment at the assessment commencement point). |
| C: The amount under Article 31(2)2 of the Act (the normal increase in land prices during the assessment period). |
| D: The amount under Article 31(2)3 of the Act (development costs incurred for the waterfront area development project). |

Article 25 (Financial Resources of the Fund)
"Revenue prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 32, subparagraph 5 of the Act means money borrowed at the expense of the River Management Fund under Article 30 of the Act.

Article 26 (Uses of the Fund)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 33, subparagraph 4 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Costs of investigations, research and development for river works, maintenance and repair.
2. Expenditure for conservation and improvement of surrounding areas that need to be managed systematically and in a planned manner in connection with rivers.

Article 27 (Waterfront Area Development Committee)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 37(1)6 of the Act means matters that the chairperson of the Waterfront Area Development Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") considers necessary and submits to a meeting of the Committee.
(2) The members of the Committee shall be the following persons: <Amended March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; June 8, 2018; December 28, 2021; October 1, 2025; December 30, 2025>
1. The Vice Minister of the Interior and Safety; a Vice Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism designated by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism; a Vice Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment designated by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment; and the Vice Minister of Planning and Budget.
2. Persons appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among persons falling under the subparagraphs of Article 37(3) of the Act.
3. Persons appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among persons recommended by the heads of relevant central administrative agencies as having extensive specialized knowledge and experience in river management, urban planning, the environment or similar fields.
(3) The term of office of commissioned members under paragraph (2) shall be two years, and they may be recommissioned only once.
(4) The chairperson of the Committee shall convene its meetings and preside over them.
(5) A meeting of the Committee shall open with a majority of all incumbent members present, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.
(6) At a member's request or where considered necessary, the chairperson may have interested parties, experts and others attend a meeting and speak.
(7) Interested parties, experts and others attending the Committee may be paid allowances, travel expenses and other necessary expenses within budgetary limits. However, this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends the Committee in direct connection with the official's duties.
(8) Except as provided in this Decree, matters necessary for operation of the Committee shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 28 (Exclusion, Challenge and Recusal of Members)
(1) A member of the Committee (hereinafter referred to as a "member") shall be excluded from the Committee's deliberation and resolution in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member, the member's spouse or former spouse is a party to the relevant matter (including an officer where the party is a corporation, organization or similar entity; hereinafter the same shall apply in this subparagraph and subparagraph 2), or is a joint holder of rights or joint obligor with a party to that matter.
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the relevant matter.
3. Where the member has provided advice, research, services (including subcontracted services), appraisal or investigation concerning the relevant matter.
4. Where the member, or a corporation, organization or similar entity to which the member belongs, is or was an agent of a party to the relevant matter.
5. Where an enterprise or similar entity in which the member serves as an officer or employee, or served within the last three years, has provided advice, research, services (including subcontracted services), appraisal or investigation concerning the relevant matter.
(2) A party to the relevant matter may apply to the Committee to challenge a member where circumstances make it difficult to expect fair deliberation and resolution from that member, and the Committee shall decide by resolution. In such cases, the challenged member shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) Where a member falls under any ground for exclusion in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the member shall voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution of the relevant matter.

Article 29 (Dismissal and Decommissioning of Members)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may dismiss or decommission a member of the Committee under Article 27(2)2 or 3 in any of the following cases: <Amended June 8, 2018; October 1, 2025>
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties due to a mental or physical disability.
2. Where misconduct relating to the member's duties is found.
3. Where the member is considered unsuitable due to neglect of duties, loss of dignity or other reasons.
4. Where the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite falling under any subparagraph of Article 28(1).
5. Where the member expresses that it is difficult to perform the duties.
